Over the last 15 minutes, buy SOL (69.95) exceeded sell SOL (54.85), with net inflow of +15.1 SOL and 136 new buyers, so demand was still arriving at the time of the decision. Pool depth of 61 SOL is workable for a $20 ticket.

But the case is weak. The 30-minute return is -48% and the drawdown from the high is 62%, which is the profile of a coin already bleeding. The first two minutes after graduation show a sell-to-buy ratio above 1.0 and a launch bot present, so early buyers were already exiting. The 15-minute return of +65% is a short bounce inside a larger decline, and the latest window's buying (136 buyers) is far below the curve's earlier pace. Nothing here shows that demand will persist 30-60 minutes out, and the base rate for a recently graduated coin in this state is a loss. Honest verdict: no strong case; skip unless you're willing to accept a likely loss on a $20 ticket.

Sell-to-buy in the first two minutes after graduation was 1.04, meaning early buyers were already exiting, and a launch bot was present. The pool is only 61 SOL deep, so a $20 round trip at 1.4-5.1% fees plus impact is painful if the bounce fades. Net flow over the last 15 minutes is positive, but 125 sellers against 136 buyers shows no conviction.
